svg.title: Unexpected event and a slower participant without Event Mode
svg.desc: With a one-second base step, a fast source returns at 1.2 seconds. A factor-three ordinary target has already stepped from zero to three. A replay-safe checkpoint permits restoration to zero and replay to 1.2, followed by a step to three with the changed input. Without a checkpoint the target stays at three, warns and uses the changed input on its next step from three. The complete text trace accompanies the figure.
svg.text: Event at 1.2 s: source factor 1, ordinary target factor 3
Blue: actual step; dashed amber: advance later discarded on restore; red: event/input change.
The first target step is already complete when the event is discovered. Time runs left to right.
Execution boundaries: 0, 1, 1.2, 2, 3 s. The request starting at 1 s returns early.
Target with checkpoint and safe replay
Target without usable checkpoint or safe replay
0 to 3: input 0; next step from 3 uses input 7
Warning: the target could not be rewound. A later staged sample can replace the event sample.
Input application is not the same as event occurrence; replay does not add Event Mode to the target.
Without Event Mode, the target applies staged inputs when it can take its next valid normal step.
